# S167 — Spec check on a single-slice launch

**Findings:**  · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**2026-10-29** — Owner decisions 2026-10-29 (interactive): if the spec check itself fails the launch is blocked, as waves do (no skip flag). Split: this slice keeps the daemon gate (run.start gated by specGate) and ork run; the Roadmap launch sitting moves to the new TUI slice, which runs after S166.

trust: unverified; by: Jon R

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

The spec check runs only at wave launch. The daemon method `spec.check` is called by `l` in Waves (`internal/tui/waves.go:388`, `internal/tui/speccheck.go:62-78`) and by `ork wave start` (`internal/cli/wave.go:160,238-296`). `ork run` and the Roadmap launch never call it: `runSlice` goes from the plan to `run.start` (`internal/cli/run.go:107-135`) and `startLaunch` sends `run.start` with no check (`internal/tui/launch.go:190-213`). The daemon refuses an item with open questions only inside `wave.start` (`specGate`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:637`, `internal/daemon/speccheck.go:339-363`), not on `run.start` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1076-1085`). So a one-off slice can start on a thin spec that a wave would have held.

Parity row: 1.2 (check that a spec is ready) and gap 2 of the prioritized list in `docs/orchestrator-parity.md` (from S165).

Owner decisions that apply:
- The spec check is one read-only pass of the spec-check role; it asks structured questions, the owner answers in one sitting, ork appends an `Owner decisions (date)` paragraph with `slicer edit --append` and files keyed questions in adj only when the project has adj and the owner turned filing on (adj 164 roles.spec-check; `docs/design.md:188-212`). Spec check verdicts are an in-memory job cache tied to a fingerprint of the spec; ork stores no verdict (`docs/boundaries.md:18`).
- ork calls the slicer CLI for the row (`slicer relay-roles`, rule "Spec check row (rNN)") and for `edit`; it reimplements nothing (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:89-124`).
- The role is read-only and edits nothing; filling a thin spec is S179 (v1.1), not this slice.

Slicer check (`slicer find "spec check" --root ../slicer`): slicer provides the matrix row and the `edit --append` command (s392, s399, s400, all done); it has no launch-time check. ork already calls them for waves; this slice only adds the call to the two single-slice launch paths.

Cost to note: one spec-check role run per unchecked or changed spec, as for a wave. An item already checked and unchanged is answered from the daemon cache at no cost (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:166-171`).

Design (*proposed*): the check runs after the plan and before the start confirmation, the same place as in a wave. `ork run` prints the sitting on stdin and stdout (stderr with `--json`); the Roadmap launch shows the same sitting as Waves. An item whose questions stay open is held: `ork run` exits 1 with `held`, the Roadmap launch closes with a status line. The daemon also refuses `run.start` for an item whose current spec has open questions (`spec_questions`), so a script cannot skip the check by calling the wire.

Not in this slice: filling or drafting a spec (S179), a flag or key that skips the check (see Open), changing the spec-check prompt or its lineup, the wave path.

## Failing tests

- `TestRunStartRefusesAnItemWithOpenSpecQuestions` (`internal/daemon/speccheck_test.go`): after a check that left questions, `run.start` for that item returns code `spec_questions` and starts nothing.
- `TestRunStartDoesNotRefuseAnItemNeverChecked`: an unchecked item, or one whose spec changed since the check, still starts, as `specGate` allows for waves.
- `TestSingleRunCarriesSpecAnswersIntoTheBrief`: answers recorded by `spec.answer` reach the single run's implementer brief and run record (`decisions`).
- `TestRunCallsTheSpecCheckAfterThePlanAndBeforeConfirmation` (`internal/cli/run_test.go`): call order is `run.plan`, `spec.check`, the confirmation, `run.start`; `--yes` still calls `spec.check`.
- `TestRunAsksSpecQuestionsOnStdinThenStarts`: a number picks an option, text is the answer, `spec.answer` gets the answers, and `run.start` follows.
- `TestRunHoldsAnItemWhoseQuestionsStayOpen`: an empty line or end of input exits 1, prints `held: S1 has N open spec questions`, and never calls `run.start`.
- `TestRunSpecCheckErrorStopsBeforeStart`: a `spec.check` error (for example no Spec check row) exits 1 with the code and message, and never calls `run.start`.
- `TestRunJSONKeepsTheSittingOffStdout`: with `--json` the questions go to stderr, stdout is one value, and a held item prints `{"started":false,"held":["S1"]}`.
- `TestLaunchRunsTheSpecCheckBeforeTheConfirmation` (`internal/tui/launch_test.go`): after the plan, the status shows `pending: spec.check`; a ready item goes to the confirmation.
- `TestLaunchSittingAnswersRecordThenConfirm`: questions open one sitting; `1`-`N`, `t` and `enter` answer; the last answer calls `SpecAnswer`; the confirmation follows.
- `TestLaunchSittingSkipClosesTheLaunchWithAStatus`: `s` or `esc` closes the launch with `S90 waits on N spec questions`, and no Start.
- `TestLaunchSittingGolden`: the sitting on the launch at 100x30, colour and mono (`launch-sitting-100x30-color.txt`, `-mono.txt`).

## Implement

UI slice: UI pass (r14). Test-first: write the tests above; the existing `run` tests will also fail until their stubs answer `spec.check`. Then:
1. `internal/daemon/runs.go:1076-1085`: in `handleRun`, before `d.startRun` for `MethodRunStart`, call `d.specGate(ctx, p.Project, p.Item)` (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:339`). `startWave` keeps its own gate (`:637`), which gives the per-item error; the single path gets it here, so the gate runs once on each path. No new wire method.
2. `internal/cli/run.go`: after the plan is printed (`:113-119`) and before the confirmation (`:120`), call the existing `a.specCheck(ctx, o, reader, prompts, &daemon.WaveStartParams{Items: []daemon.RunParams{params}})` (`internal/cli/wave.go:238`). If it returns no item, print `held`, and exit `ExitFailure`; with `--json` print `{"started":false,"held":[ITEM]}` as `wave.go:169` does. A non-zero code from it is returned as is. Move `specCheck` and `askSpecQuestions` to `internal/cli/speccheck.go` (new) only if that keeps `wave.go` readable; no logic change.
3. Existing stubs: make `runPrompted` (`internal/cli/run_test.go:35-44`) and the `Call` stubs in `TestRunShowsPlanBeforeConfirmation` and `TestRunYesStartsAndOwnerCommands` answer `spec.check` with `{"items":[{"item":"S1","ready":true}]}`.
4. TUI state: the sitting, the in-flight flag, the answers cache and the owner-needed text now live on `wavesState` (`internal/tui/waves.go:54-58`). Move them into a `specState` that both `wavesState` and `launchState` hold. `sittingKey`, `answerSitting`, `endSitting`, `finishSitting`, `applyAnswer` and `sittingParts` (`internal/tui/speccheck.go:144-340`) take the `specState` and a done callback (waves: `askLaunch`, launch: confirm). Waves behaviour and its goldens must not change; `TestWavesLaunchRunsTheSpecCheckBeforeTheConfirmation` (`internal/tui/speccheck_test.go:42`) is the guard.
5. `internal/tui/launch.go`: add stages `launchSpecPending` and `launchSitting` between `launchPlanPending` and `launchConfirm` (`:20-27`). In `applyLaunch` (`:252-254`) a new plan starts `live.SpecCheck(ctx, project, []string{item})` instead of the confirmation; a reply is a `launchSpecMsg` matched by `l.request`. Ready: set `m.confirm` as before. Questions: open the sitting. Sitting ended with the item ready: confirm. Skipped: `dropLaunch`, status `ITEM waits on N spec questions; l checks again`. A check error drops the launch and shows its code and message verbatim (as plan errors do, `:242-246`). A re-plan after an S166 edit does not check again.
6. `internal/tui/model.go:447-452,525-529` (paste and key routing), `internal/tui/keys.go:253-267` (hints) and `internal/tui/view.go:95-96` (`launchView` draws `sittingParts` in stage `launchSitting`): route to whichever of waves or launch holds the sitting.
7. `internal/tui/live_test.go:230` and `launchLive` (`internal/tui/launch_test.go:24`): the launch tests' fake answers `SpecCheck` ready by default, as `wavesLive` does (`internal/tui/waves_test.go:41`).
8. Docs: `docs/design.md:186-200` (the check also runs on `ork run` and the Roadmap launch) and `:974-996`, `docs/dashboard.md:1124-1170` and `:1275-1331`, `docs/guide.md` sections 7 and 9 (S165).
9. Goldens: `go test ./internal/tui -update`; review `testdata/golden/` (only the two launch-sitting files are new).
Order: the TUI part comes after S166 (same files, `internal/tui/launch.go`, `model.go`); the daemon and CLI parts are independent. S168 and S169 do not touch these paths.
Size: the label is S; steps 4 to 6 (moving the sitting out of Waves) make it closer to M. If the owner wants S, split: S167a is steps 1 to 3 (daemon gate and `ork run`), S167b is steps 4 to 9 (Roadmap launch).
Open: a spec-check failure (no Spec check row in the matrix, or the vendor fails) blocks the launch, as it does for `ork wave start` today. Options: (a) block, no skip (recommended: same rule as waves, nothing starts unchecked); (b) warn and start anyway; (c) add `--skip-spec-check` to `ork run` and nothing in the TUI.
